evals.name: backend-prisma-create-endpoint
evals.prompt: Write tests for a POST /api/bookings endpoint that creates a new booking. The booking needs a userId, roomId, startTime, and endTime. If the room is already booked during that time range, it should return 409. The project uses NestJS + Prisma + PostgreSQL + Vitest. There's a Booking model in the Prisma schema with those fields plus an 'id' (autoincrement) and 'createdAt' timestamp. There's also a User and Room model. Don't write the implementation — just the test file.
evals.expected_output: A complete test file that: (1) uses vi.useFakeTimers for createdAt assertions, (2) sets up User and Room via prisma.user.create/prisma.room.create (NOT via API), (3) makes POST request via supertest, (4) asserts status 201 + response body, (5) queries prisma.booking.findUnique to verify DB persistence, (6) has a conflict test that creates an overlapping booking first then asserts 409 + no second booking in DB, (7) has an unauthenticated test asserting 401

assertions.name: uses-entity-setup-not-api
assertions.description: Test data (users, rooms) created via prisma.*.create(), not via API calls

assertions.name: has-entity-validate
assertions.description: After the POST, queries the database (prisma.booking.findUnique or similar) and asserts the record exists

assertions.name: has-entity-non-existence-on-error
assertions.description: The 409 conflict test verifies no duplicate booking was created in the DB

assertions.name: uses-time-control
assertions.description: Uses vi.useFakeTimers() and vi.setSystemTime() for deterministic timestamp testing

assertions.name: uses-supertest-not-fetch
assertions.description: Uses supertest (request(app.getHttpServer())) for HTTP calls, not raw fetch

assertions.name: has-auth-test
assertions.description: Includes a test for unauthenticated access (401)

assertions.name: correct-test-structure
assertions.description: Uses describe/it blocks with success and failure case groupings

evals.name: drizzle-hono-stack-detection
evals.expected_output: Tests that use Hono's app.request() (NOT supertest), Drizzle's db.insert/db.select for entity setup and validation, correct Drizzle query syntax (eq() from drizzle-orm), and follow all six instructions

assertions.name: uses-hono-request
assertions.description: Uses app.request() or similar Hono test pattern, NOT supertest

assertions.name: uses-drizzle-for-setup
assertions.description: EntitySetup uses db.insert(table).values() with Drizzle syntax

assertions.name: uses-drizzle-for-validation
assertions.description: EntityValidate uses db.select().from(table).where(eq()) with Drizzle syntax

assertions.name: parses-json-response
assertions.description: Correctly parses Hono's Response object via .json() (not accessing .body directly like supertest)

assertions.name: has-entity-validate-after-create
assertions.description: After POST, queries the expenses table to verify the record was persisted

assertions.name: has-validation-error-test
assertions.description: Tests missing amount/categoryId returns 400 and nothing persisted

evals.name: review-catches-missing-db-validation
evals.expected_output: Should flag: (1) CRITICAL: test data setup via API (beforeAll creates user via POST, should use prisma.user.create), (2) CRITICAL: no EntityValidate after successful POST (never checks if order exists in DB), (3) HIGH: no EntityNonExistenceValidate on error case (400 test doesn't verify no order was created), (4) HIGH: hardcoded totalPrice (29.98) is brittle, (5) MEDIUM: no time control if order has createdAt

assertions.name: flags-api-setup-coupling
assertions.description: Identifies that the user is created via API call (POST /api/users) instead of direct DB insert

assertions.name: flags-missing-entity-validate
assertions.description: Points out that the successful create test never queries the DB to verify the order was persisted

assertions.name: flags-missing-non-existence-check
assertions.description: Points out that the error case test doesn't verify no order was accidentally created

assertions.name: suggests-prisma-create
assertions.description: Suggests using prisma.user.create() for setup instead of the API call

assertions.name: uses-severity-levels
assertions.description: Uses severity indicators (CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, etc.) to prioritize findings

evals.name: bug-fix-gear-no-ceremony
evals.prompt: Users are reporting that when they update their profile email, the old email is returned in the response but the new email is saved in the database. The endpoint is PATCH /api/users/profile and it uses NestJS + Prisma. Can you help me write a test that reproduces this bug?
evals.expected_output: Should NOT demand PRDs, specs, or the full three-spec ceremony. Should immediately guide writing a reproducing test: (1) EntitySetup for a user, (2) PATCH request with new email, (3) ResponseValidate checking the response has the NEW email, (4) EntityValidate querying the DB to verify the NEW email is stored, (5) the test should capture the exact bug described — response shows old email while DB has new email

assertions.name: no-spec-ceremony
assertions.description: Does NOT ask for PRDs, acceptance criteria, or demand creating an OpenAPI spec first

assertions.name: reproduces-the-specific-bug
assertions.description: The test specifically checks that the response email matches the updated email (catching the reported discrepancy)

assertions.name: has-both-response-and-db-check
assertions.description: Test checks both the API response AND the database, which is exactly how to diagnose this bug

assertions.name: uses-entity-setup
assertions.description: Creates the initial user via prisma.user.create, not via API

evals.name: vue-component-test-with-store
evals.prompt: Write a component test for this Vue 3 component. It's a leave request form where employees can submit leave. Uses Pinia for state management. The LeaveRequestForm.vue component has a date picker (start/end date), a reason textarea, and a submit button. When submitted, it calls the store's submitLeaveRequest action. Write the test using Vitest + @vue/test-utils.
evals.expected_output: Component test that: (1) mounts with createTestingPinia, (2) seeds initial store state, (3) fills the form fields, (4) clicks submit, (5) asserts BOTH the rendered success message AND the store action was called with correct arguments. Should NOT use the backend six-instruction names literally — should adapt to frontend terminology.

assertions.name: uses-testing-pinia
assertions.description: Mounts with createTestingPinia({ createSpy: vi.fn })

assertions.name: seeds-store-state
assertions.description: Seeds the Pinia store with initial state (e.g., current user)

assertions.name: asserts-rendered-output
assertions.description: Checks the DOM/rendered text after interaction (ResponseValidate equivalent)

assertions.name: asserts-store-state
assertions.description: Checks the store action was called or store state changed (EntityValidate equivalent — verifies the data layer, not just the UI)

assertions.name: uses-data-testid-or-accessible-selectors
assertions.description: Uses data-testid attributes or accessible selectors, not CSS class names
